prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks, in which magic-wavelength trapping enabled many-atom frequency standards at the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I keep optical lattice clocks as my preferred configuration after the full round-1 exchange. The distinguishing physics is the magic-wavelength condition: a trapping potential whose light shift cancels for the clock transition, so that very many atoms can be held in the Lamb-Dicke regime and interrogated together. That is what changed the statistical regime of optical frequency standards, and it is why lattice clocks now reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and the stability that only many-atom averaging gives. It has been reproduced independently with Sr, Yb and Hg in several national laboratories, and it underlies the discussion of a redefinition of the second, centimetre-scale relativistic geodesy and sensitive tests of constant variation. The credit is the cleanest on the shortlist: Katori proposed the principle and Ye's group drove it to record accuracy and stability, two names with a clear proposal-plus-realisation division. The chair asked whether a lattice-clock prize is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. My answer is that those honoured the toolkit and a different platform, while this one honours a new trapping principle for neutral atoms; I would draft the citation around that principle and not around the clock records, which keep moving.
statement.case_against: The reservations that remain are real. A prize may be read as a third award in precision measurement after 1997, 2005 and 2012, and the headline application, a redefined second, has not happened yet. Katori's priority relative to other early lattice-clock proposers, including the Lemonde group, and the roles of the JILA and Tokyo teams are not settled by the supplied record, and I am relying on recalled history; a two-name prize will leave out strong contributors. B048 has clearly broader opening support and two decades of confirmation. If the committee decides that breadth of impact across physics should outweigh a well-bounded but specialised achievement, my preference is a minority one, and B048 would be my first fallback, provided its attribution problem can be answered.

responses.point: The chair asked how to weigh breadth of opening support (seven rankers for B016, six for B048, four for B049) against depth of first-place preferences, and prefers B016 as a theory-plus-experiment chain with no recorded opposition.
responses.response: I do not treat support counts as the measure. B016 was ranked by seven members, but only as second to fifth and never first, and I myself placed it fifth. Breadth of appeal and the quality of a discovery are different questions. On the science I accept Mark's point that the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction and the 2018 discovery form a real prediction-and-confirmation chain. My difficulty is the one he lists himself: about seven years of confirmation, an unsettled pairing mechanism, and Cao and other co-first authors outside the three names. A citation limited to the flat-band prediction and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states would be accurate, but the committee would still be rewarding a field that is still defining itself. Lattice clocks have two decades of independent reproduction and a cleaner credit. I am not moved off B049, though I would rank B016 above B038 and B029 if my first choice failed.

responses.point: Mehlig says that if the committee judges the B048 attribution unresolvable within three names, B016 is the cleaner theory-plus-experiment triple, and that the 2016 overlap is partial and conceptual.
responses.response: I agree with the conditional and with his reading of 2016. Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz concerned quantum Hall physics and defect-driven transitions, not time-reversal-invariant Z2 matter, so that overlap is not by itself disqualifying. My remaining objection is the attribution. The Z2 prediction is Kane and Mele's and the observation is Molenkamp's, but the HgTe proposal that told Molenkamp where to look is Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's. A citation worded as the Z2 state and its first observation is accurate, yet it implicitly asserts that the HgTe step was incidental, and that is the dispute. I would accept that wording only if the committee agreed that the Kane-Mele prediction was the originating discovery and the HgTe theory a consequence. That is a judgement I can see members reaching, which is why B048 remains my first alternative and not a lower one.

responses.point: Olsson argues that B048 is the best-bounded discovery on the shortlist, mature after nearly twenty years, and that the committee agreement is grounded in the science and not in momentum, while naming the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap as the strongest reservation.
responses.response: The maturity and breadth arguments are strong, and I do not dispute that the discovery is textbook. The point I would press is that she calls B048 the best-bounded discovery while also naming as her strongest reservation that the proposal which made the experiment a targeted test sits outside the credited trio. Those two statements pull against each other. Bounded in what sense: as an idea (Kane and Mele), or as an experimental result (Molenkamp)? If it is the Z2 idea, the HgTe route is secondary; if it is the observed quantum spin Hall state, BHZ is part of the chain. I would want the supporters to say which they mean before the vote, because the answer decides whether three names are sufficient. I have not changed my ranking on this, but her case is the one most likely to move me.

responses.point: Kroll holds B049 first with the same clean two-name credit, and lists B020 and then B048 as alternatives, while acknowledging that as an atomic physicist he may overvalue precision-measurement advances.
responses.response: I share his argument and his caution about it. We are the two atomic physicists on the committee and have a shared bias toward measurement as discovery, so I want the case to rest on what is new in the physics: the magic-wavelength condition and the many-atom regime, both shown by independent reproduction. I differ on the second choice. He places B020 above B048; I place B048 above B020 because the atom-interferometry credit leaves out Chu and I find that gap harder to defend than the B048 gap. I also note that his disclosed JILA connection to Ye's home institution is his to weigh, and my own connections (Lund, ETH Zurich, theory collaborators) do not touch Katori or Ye.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B016 as a quantitative theory prediction followed by a decisive experiment, but accepts that the pairing mechanism and the correlated insulators are not understood and that the field is early compared with B048.
responses.response: His own list of uncertainties is the strongest case against moving to B016 now. If the mechanism and the nature of the correlated insulators are open and the experiment is seven years old, a prize rewards the existence of the phenomena and a platform. That is a defensible basis, and it is how the committee has sometimes acted, but it is less mature than a clock principle that is reproduced in several laboratories and in use. I do accept his point that a clean continuum model predicting emergent correlated physics is exactly the kind of discovery the prize should reward, and I would not oppose B016 if it were to become the committee's centre of gravity.

uncertainties: Whether the committee views lattice clocks as a distinct achievement or as continuation of the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes; I judge it distinct, but members in other fields may weigh it differently.
Katori's priority over other early lattice-clock proposers, and Ye's role relative to the JILA team, rest on recalled history and are not settled by the supplied record.
Whether the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit can be reconciled with a Kane-Mele-Molenkamp prize; this decides whether B048 or B049 is my first choice if the committee will not rank B049 first.
Whether the still-pending redefinition of the second counts as a timing signal in favour or as a reason to wait.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with Katori or Ye is apparent from my record. My documented connections are with the attosecond community (L'Huillier, Lund), Keller's group at ETH Zurich and a few theory collaborators, none of whom is credited in B049. I disclose general atomic-physics proximity for B049, B020 and B029, and a minor tie for B038 because Wallraff is at ETH Zurich where I have collaborated with a different group. I do not seek recusal. I note that Kroll's disclosed JILA connection and my own shared field proximity are factors for the committee to weigh in assessing our two statements together.
